title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Advising a Client to Ignore an Order
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities
topic: Advising a Client to Ignore an Order

questions.q: A client is dissatisfied with a recent interim order issued by an LTB adjudicator, which requires the client to pay $500 into the tribunal by a certain date. The client asks the paralegal, "Can I just ignore this order since the adjudicator is obviously biased?" What must the paralegal advise?
options: Advise the client that they can ignore the order because it is an interim order, not final.
Advise the client that they must comply with the tribunal's order, and outline the legal options for appealing or reviewing the order.
Advise the client to physically protest at the tribunal's office.
Advise the client to pay the $500 to the paralegal instead of the tribunal.
questions.explain: Under Rule 2.02 (Honesty and Candour), a paralegal must respect the administration of justice and shall not encourage or advise a client to act in a manner contrary to the law or a tribunal order. The paralegal's duty is to advise the client to comply while explaining the legal avenues available to challenge the order.
